items.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
items.summary: DeepSeek released a faster, leaner update to its V4.1 Flash open-weight model on Oct 17 with MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope. It improves reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks while cutting per-task cost roughly 60% versus its predecessor, intensifying the open-weight race against US frontier labs.

items.name: Reflection AI Beam
items.summary: Reflection AI released Beam on Oct 16, its first open-weight model: a 501B-total / 23B-active sparse MoE for coding, reasoning, and long-horizon agents under Apache 2.0. It launched with day-zero support across 40+ partners plus the open-sourced Mirror terminal agent harness, making it the largest Apache-2.0 frontier-class release from a US lab.

items.name: Meta Muse Spark Open
items.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Spark Open on Oct 15: an 816B-total / 42B-active natively multimodal MoE with 1M-token context, which Meta calls the most capable US open-weight model to date. Built for coding and agentic work, it debuted across 7 inference providers and was demoed running on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX.

items.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Oct 15: an open 120B-total / 12B-active vision-language MoE for specialized always-on agents, handling text, images, documents, and video. NVIDIA claims leading accuracy at one-fifth the parameter count of its largest reasoning model and 5x throughput in its class, alongside two new Bolt edge models.

items.name: Google Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google opened its new frontier model Gemini 4 Argon to developers on Oct 13 via the Gemini API and AI Studio, and to AI Pro/Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. Built for deep-reasoning, long-horizon software engineering, legal, finance, and cybersecurity defense workflows, it launched at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens intro pricing.
